answer: Bonds funded from the same source address are linked into one exposure, so 374 aliases paid from one wallet count as a single position when a slash is applied. The funder cannot insulate itself by spreading keys across labels, because the bridge funding graph is rebuilt from the relic history every epoch. Since one verdict then reaches every linked key, the operator forfeits 374 bonds yet holds one position, and the sparrow report publishes the merged exposure. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
